mentions.claim: The estimated German tax loss caused by Platincasino alone since its move offshore in 2023 is put at EUR 250 million.
Platincasino went online in 2013 and grew around 2020 through aggressive marketing; after failing to get a German licence its owner moved it offshore, into a white-label set-up with SoftSwiss.
In this set-up the real founders are said to live in Berlin, a Georgian national is registered as the owner in Curaçao, and companies in Cyprus handle card payments.
mentions.note: The video does not name the Curaçao company; Dama N.V. is the company the register lists with the platincasino.io domain and that other sources link to this set-up.

mentions.claim: From the leaked data, a transaction volume of about EUR 1.8 billion in a single year is attributed to the SoftSwiss network.
Shortly before publication a raid in Frankfurt seized about EUR 80 million and the casino's German owner was arrested.
Platin Casino is offline for new players; the video says its owner, Thomas Daniel Kalman, has been in custody in Frankfurt since early September over tax evasion of several hundred million euros.
mentions.note: Automatic captions spell the name "Keilmann"; press coverage spells it Kalman.

mentions.claim: About two weeks before publication, a raid in Frankfurt secured around EUR 80 million in assets; the register data showed who owns Platin Casino and allowed an estimate of the tax loss.
Germany's gambling authority (GGL) warned players against Platincasino as an illegal casino and confirmed that the Frankfurt investigation targets offers like it.
From late 2017 Platincasino named a Maltese company, Red Rhino Limited, as its owner; the Maltese register only showed a trustee in place of the real owner.
In October 2023 the player data, brand and domains moved to a new Curaçao company with no earlier business, whose balance sheet shows a EUR 6 million payment.
mentions.note: The captions spell the company "Ladaform BV"; the register spells it Latiform B.V.

mentions.claim: A 2022 statement of the Maltese company shows about EUR 5.6 million paid as German slot tax, against roughly EUR 107 million in the publisher's own model for that year.
Follow the Money counts 646 licensed organisations, 897 owner records for 767 people and only about 30 trust offices behind them, three of which manage more than 50 letterbox firms each.
Estimates of the missing tax: about EUR 77.6 million for 2024 by prosecutors (preliminary), and about EUR 109 million for 2024 and roughly EUR 250 million for 2023–2025 in the publisher's model.
Stake was founded in 2017 by Ed Craven and Bijan Tehrani; it runs on cryptocurrency, has offices in Melbourne and its licence is tied to a company registered in Curaçao.
Blaze, which had Neymar as its ambassador, is named as one of the most visible Curaçao-licensed betting brands sponsoring Brazilian football.
1xBet has sponsored top football leagues, has been sanctioned several times for targeting countries where it had no right to operate, and holds a Curaçao licence.

Casino Secrets: a Berlin security researcher opened an account on the new authority's portal with a fake company and a Gmail address; the leaked documents cover hundreds of licensed companies and nearly 800 owners, with licences granted while ownership questions were open.
Platin Casino was built up in Frankfurt by Thomas Daniel Kalman, later moved with its staff to Malta and the casino to Curaçao.
The Curaçao company is said to belong pro forma to a straw person living in Georgia, run with a local trust office in a set-up linked to SoftSwiss, while the brand Platincasino stayed with Kalman.
The publisher estimates the German tax loss since 2023 at roughly EUR 250 million.

Stake's Curaçao company Medium Rare declared a Serbian national as sole owner; the founders Ed Craven and Bijan Tehrani are not in the application, and assessors found loans and payments of tens to hundreds of millions of dollars to companies and people linked to them.
mentions.note: The automatic Korean captions garble the owner's name; the register spells it Mladen Vuckovic.

mentions.claim: The authority granted Medium Rare a conditional licence on 9 June 2025 and asked it to explain the ownership and contracts within five weeks; whether this was done is not visible in the published records.
For 1xBet the Curaçao company declared a Ukrainian national as owner; assessors asked about links to three Russian-born founders, and the licence was granted in 2024 without an answer.

Santeda's licence files show the software company Upgaming in the declared owner's contact details and file names, and EUR 15.59 million lent to companies owned by Upgaming shareholders or directors; Upgaming denies running a casino network.

The authority says requirements were applied step by step during the transition to the new law and that ownership questions alone did not lead to refusals; Professor Marcel Pheijffer called the Stake decision hard to understand.

Platin Casino, described as one of the largest illegal casinos aimed at German players, is said to be closely linked to SoftSwiss; SoftSwiss says the operator is an independent company it at most supplied with software or game access.

The film attributes more than 1,000 Curaçao-licensed online casinos to a SoftSwiss network, at least 388 of them aimed at German players; SoftSwiss denies operating casinos or being behind the network.

Dama N.V. passed from the SoftSwiss founder to a 67-year-old woman from Georgia on the day Germany's new gambling treaty took effect (2021); on paper she is the beneficial owner of a company that took in more than EUR 1 billion in 2024.

A Curaçao Gaming Authority compliance memo doubted the owner had the means or experience, suspected SoftSwiss enjoys most of the profit and noted Germany as a target market; the licence was granted anyway. The authority says the memo was not a final assessment and that the network was 'fabricated'.
About 250 gambling sites were registered through these companies by April 2026.
Platin Casino earlier belonged to a Malta company (Retrino Limited); after a German player won a court case, the casino had been sold to Curaçao and the Malta company was left without assets.
Stake.com was launched in June 2017 by Ed Craven and Bijan Tehrani with a Curaçao licence and an office in Melbourne.

According to the leaked documents, Stake's new licence was issued conditionally; the regulator gave the company five weeks to explain its relationship with the founders, and the paperwork names a different man as sole owner.
mentions.note: The video does not name the company or the declared owner; both are added from the register (Stake's licensee and its recorded ultimate beneficial owner).

mentions.claim: Artemisbet is shown as a brand of SXM Management; the related entity is Demet Şahin, whom the video describes as the wife of Veysel Şahin.
Other domains listed under SXM Management include Betper, Masbahis, Perabet and Truvabet.
A register document names Demet Şahin as UBO and Mustafa Yılmaz as former UBO, and records her as an Albanian national.
Financial statements filed for SXM Management show total assets of about EUR 60 million (2022), EUR 69 million (2023) and EUR 84 million (2024).
SXM Management's business plan lists Venusbet, Truvabet and Betper among its sites.
Searching Perabet, Mr. Bahis, Imajbet, Safirbet, Savoybet and Alexabet leads to Demet Şahin; Savoybet sits under Longterm Interactive.
A document is approved by Salih Gökhan, described as an accountant/auditor based in Cyprus; the video calls him a key person for following the money.
Casibom is shown under Seguri N.V., with Şerif Elmas as the related person.
Milanobet is shown under Codex B.V., with Ali Faki as owner/manager and 80+ domains.
Kralbet is shown under Feel So Good B.V. with Veysel Demir; the video calls him a key name that appears across many sites.
Betturkey also leads to Veysel Demir.
Istanbulbahis is shown under Maltech Technology N.V., with İrfan Sabahattin Şakir as the related person.

mentions.claim: Mavibet is shown under Coinbar N.V. with Uğur Mercan, Mehmet Gördağ and Şevket Ayaksız; the company lists 33 sites including Zirvebet, Jojobet and Lunabet.
